bluetooth_confirm.title: Kirri Beacon Diffuser
bluetooth_confirm.description:
Set up the Kirri Beacon Diffuser at {address}?

Home Assistant will connect once to confirm it really is a Beacon — the diffuser only advertises a generic service UUID that many other devices also use, so this check is the only way to be sure.

user.title: Kirri Beacon Diffuser
user.description:
Enter the diffuser's Bluetooth address.

If it is not listed automatically, check it is switched on — after a power cut the Beacon stays off until its base button is pressed by hand.

data_description.address: Six pairs of hex digits, e.g. AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF

error.invalid_address: That is not a Bluetooth address. Expected six colon-separated pairs of hex digits.
error.cannot_connect: The diffuser is not reachable. Check it is switched on at the base and that the Bluetooth proxy near it is online.
error.not_supported: Something answered at that address, but it is not a Kirri Beacon — it does not have the vendor service.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. Check the Home Assistant log.

abort.already_configured: This diffuser is already set up.
abort.cannot_connect: The diffuser is not reachable. Check it is switched on at the base and that the Bluetooth proxy near it is online.
abort.not_supported: This device advertises the same generic service as the Kirri Beacon but is not one.
abort.unknown: Unexpected error. Check the Home Assistant log.

data_description.poll_interval: Only a safety net — the diffuser confirms every change immediately, and availability comes from its advertisements. Long intervals cost nothing.
data_description.drain_seconds: How long to hold the Bluetooth link after a command, so a follow-up does not pay for another connection. Each connection takes 3–5 seconds.
